text:
drunk Alice yesterday

gave me

a jar of fig jam

and today she

whistles

for her cat

but

he will not

come—

he is with the horses

in a

tub of beer

or

in room 21

of the

Crown Hill

Hotel

or he is in the

Cracker

Citizens National

Bank

or

arrived in

New York at

5:30 p.m.

with a paper suitcase

and

7 dollars.

near Alice

in her yard

a paper goose

walks

upside down

in a cardboard box that says:

California

Oranges.

the drunk Alice whistles.

not well not well.

work slowly.

everyone tries hard

but the

gods.

Alice goes in for a

drink, comes

out,

whistles again

all the way to a

park bench in

El Paso—

and her love comes

running from the

trees

eyes shining like a

color film

and not waiting

until

Monday

we go in

together.

translation.title: Drunk Alice Yesterday...
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The supplied opening phrase functions as a title, and its trailing ellipsis has been retained. The duplicated Spanish ‘vendrá / venir-’ is normalized by context as ‘will not / come—.’
